verdict.line: You lose if you stand and trade autos into his Ground Slam and Granite Shield; you win if you use Hookshot to pick your fights instead of his.

brief.thesis: This is a genuinely even lane at 50.4% over 1294 games because neither side has a clean statistical edge, but the tools that produce that number are asymmetric: Malphite's Ground Slam (E) punishes Camille for trading autos in melee, while Camille's Hookshot (E) and Tactical Sweep (W) let her choose engagements from range instead of slugging it out. Malphite carries the early solo-kill risk because his Q and E come online with no setup required; Camille closes the gap once Trinity Force lets her one-cycle a trade before he can reset.

theirWindow.when: Granite Shield charged and Brutal Strikes (W) active
theirWindow.what: He just took a free hit of armor/AD from Brutal Strikes and his passive shield has recharged because he hasn't been hit recently — disengage rather than trade autos here, since Ground Slam will also be up to cut your attack speed.

yourWindow.when: Ground Slam (E) on cooldown, no shield up
yourWindow.what: With his 7s E down and Granite Shield stripped from recent pokes, commit Precision Protocol (Q) into an auto and either walk away or follow with Hookshot (E) to the nearest wall — you get a clean burst window he can't answer with attack-speed reduction.

start.why: 49.1% win rate over 643 games — the extra damage lets you actually threaten a trade before Ground Slam's attack-speed cut makes prolonged autoing pointless.

boots.why: 49.3% win rate over 829 games and 62.7% pick — his magic damage comes from both E (Ground Slam) and R (Unstoppable Force), so magic resist plus tenacity softens the knock-up all-in.

core.why: The damage and move speed spike is what turns your Q-into-auto trades into real threats instead of pokes he shrugs off with Granite Shield.
Sustain and cleave let you win extended skirmishes even when Ground Slam has cut your attack speed.

runes.keystoneWhy: Grasp procs off your first hit regardless of attack speed, so it keeps working even after Ground Slam slows your attacks — and the max-health damage and heal win the extended trades this matchup produces.

summoners.why: 48.6% win rate, the best of the three combos on record — since the lane is even rather than a kill lane, Teleport lets you take side-wave priority and return with tempo instead of forcing risky all-ins into his early kill pressure.

playing.title: Bait Ground Slam before you commit
playing.detail: Ground Slam is only a 7s cooldown at 400 range — stand just outside it or let him waste it on a minion wave, then commit your Q-into-auto trade once it's down so your attack speed isn't cut mid-fight.

playing.title: Delay your Q recast for max damage
playing.detail: Precision Protocol's second cast does significantly more bonus damage the longer you wait before recasting — hold it out in trades instead of double-tapping instantly.

playing.title: Strip Granite Shield before all-in
playing.detail: His passive shield only recharges if he hasn't been hit recently — keep landing pokes so it's down when you go for the real combo instead of eating it for free.

playing.title: Don't stand in Brutal Strikes range
playing.detail: Once he activates W for the Armor/AD buff and multi-unit hit, back out past 400 range rather than trading through it.

playing.title: Save Hookshot for after level 6
playing.detail: Unstoppable Force lets him engage from 1000 range and knock you up — keep Hookshot's 16-12s cooldown available for repositioning rather than burning it on cooldown.

playing.title: Lean on Tactical Sweep to poke, not autos
playing.detail: W's outer-half slow, bonus damage, and self-heal win extended exchanges without you needing to stand in his attack range at all.

playing.title: Time Ultimatum to his ultimate, not before
playing.detail: Hextech Ultimatum dashes to and anchors him in place — use it after he's already thrown Unstoppable Force so he can't disengage the fight he started.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win rates are measured from live games on the current patch (16.18.1); the mechanical reasoning — why to bait Ground Slam, when to delay Q, how to use Hookshot to avoid trading autos — is our own tactical read on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Malphite’s (E) slows your attack speed, making it difficult to engage evenly. Use Camille’s [P] and Hookshot[E] to hit and run.
